summary: This is a well-scoped, additive gap-closure PR (tiered SLA policies/team routing, email-to-ticket promotion, public self-service portal) that follows this codebase's established conventions closely: RLS policies mirror the existing app_runtime/service_role_bypass pattern, the public-portal write path reuses the org-join-code rate-limit precedent and the conversationGuestAccess mechanism instead of inventing a new one, the escalation/SLA-breach cron is wired into the existing metric-alerts cron rather than a new one, and the manual slaHours override path in createTicket is left byte-for-byte unchanged for backward compatibility. Unit tests for the pure SLA-scoring and business-hours deadline math are genuine and pass. Does not touch .github/workflows/**. One real, concrete defect found: the new sla_policies.priority column is declared in schema.ts as the existing Postgres enum type (priorityEnum, i.e. compliance.priority, the same enum tickets.priority already uses), but the hand-written migration 0264 creates that column as plain text with a CHECK constraint instead of compliance.priority -- a schema/migration type mismatch that will surface as drift the next time drizzle-kit generate runs, in a repo that has already had serious, repeated migration-drift incidents. Functionally the CHECK constraint enforces the same value set so runtime inserts won't break, but this should be corrected (use the enum type) before or shortly after merge. Given tier2's own gate, this still requires human sign-off regardless; recommend the human reviewer also confirm CI's Type Check job passes (full-repo tsc could not be run in the worker's sandbox due to OOM) and that get_advisors(security) is run against the new public-portal RLS before/at deploy, both of which the PR's own PROGRESS.md already discloses as outstanding.
issues: drizzle/0264_helpdesk_tiered_sla_team_routing.sql declares compliance.sla_policies.priority as plain text + CHECK constraint, but src/lib/db/schema.ts declares it with priorityEnum('priority') (the compliance.priority enum type also used by tickets.priority) -- a schema/migration type mismatch that should be fixed to use the enum type for consistency and to avoid drizzle-kit drift

Admin CRUD routes for ticket-teams/sla-policies/escalation-rules/business-hours-schedules only call requireAuth() with no role/permission check, unlike the analogous departments admin-config routes which do check role -- any authenticated org member can reconfigure SLA policies and escalation routing for the whole org; worth confirming this matches intended access control before/at merge

Full-repo tsc --noEmit and get_advisors(security) were not run in the worker's sandbox (disclosed in PROGRESS.md) -- must be verified by CI / a human before merge, with particular attention to the new public-portal RLS posture
